facts.statement: The first examples of Pachyrhinosaurus were discovered by Charles M. Sternberg in Alberta, Canada, in 1946, and the genus was named in 1950.
facts.quote: The first examples were discovered by Charles M. Sternberg in Alberta, Canada, in 1946, and named in 1950.

facts.statement: Pachyrhinosaurus lakustai lived from about 73.5 to 72.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: P. lakustai, from the Wapiti Formation, the bonebed horizon of which is roughly equivalent in age to the upper Bearpaw and lower Horseshoe Canyon Formations, is known to have existed from about 73.5–72.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: Pachyrhinosaurus canadensis lived from about 73 to 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: P. canadensis is younger, known from the lower Horseshoe Canyon Formation, about 73–71 Ma ago and the St. Mary River Formation.

facts.statement: Pachyrhinosaurus perotorum lived about 73 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossils of the northernmost species, P. perotorum, have been recovered from the Prince Creek Formation of Alaska, and date to 73 Ma ago.

facts.statement: The holotype and paratype skulls of P. canadensis were collected in 1945 and 1946 from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: These skulls were collected in 1945 and 1946 from the sandy clay of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: A large bonebed of Pachyrhinosaurus was found in 1974 by Al Lakusta along Pipestone Creek in Alberta.
facts.quote: In 1974, Grande Prairie, Alberta science teacher Al Lakusta found a large bonebed along Pipestone Creek in Alberta.

facts.statement: The presence of skeletons ranging from juveniles to adults in the Pipestone Creek bonebed suggests that Pachyrhinosaurus cared for its young.
facts.quote: Found amongst the fossils were the skeletons of four distinct age groups ranging from juveniles to full-grown dinosaurs, indicating that the Pachyrhinosaurus cared for their young.

facts.statement: Adult Pachyrhinosaurus skulls featured both convex and concave bosses and unicorn-style horns on the parietal bone behind the eyes.
facts.quote: The adult skulls had both convex and concave bosses as well as unicorn-style horns on the parietal bone just behind their eyes.

facts.statement: In 2008, Philip J. Currie, Wann Langston Jr., and Darren Tanke classified the Pipestone Creek specimen as the second species, P. lakustai, named after its discoverer Al Lakusta.
facts.quote: In 2008, a detailed monograph describing the skull of the Pipestone Creek pachyrhinosaur, and penned by Philip J. Currie, Wann Langston Jr., and Darren Tanke, classified the specimen as a second species of Pachyrhinosaurus, named P. lakustai after its discoverer.

facts.statement: In 2024, a 138 cm long skull of P. lakustai with a 43 cm diameter nasal boss was unearthed at Pipestone Creek and nicknamed "Big Sam".
facts.quote: In 2024, excavation at Pipestone Creek by the Philip J. Currie Dinosaur Museum unearthed one of the largest known P. lakustai skulls. The specimen came to be known as "Big Sam" (PCB.2024.666). The 138 cm long skull has a nasal boss that is 43 cm in diameter.

facts.statement: Pachyrhinosaurus perotorum was described in 2012 and named after Texas oil billionaire Ross Perot.
facts.quote: In 2012, Fiorillo & Tykoski described Pachyrhinosaurus perotorum. This Alaskan species was named after the Texas oil billionaire and benefactor, Ross Perot.

facts.statement: The nasal boss of P. perotorum bore a thick, cornified pad and sheath, representing a unique integumentary feature not seen in other species.
facts.quote: Of note, the authors pointed out that the posterior part of the nasal shows evidence for "a degree of integument complexity not previously recognized in other species" of Pachyrhinosaurus. It was determined that the dorsal surface of the nasal boss bore a thick, cornified pad and sheath.

facts.statement: The largest species, P. canadensis, is estimated to reach lengths of 6 to 8 meters and weigh 3 to 4 tonnes.
facts.quote: Size estimates for the largest Pachyrhinosaurus species, P. canadensis indicate lengths of 6-8 m and a weight of 3-4 tonne.

facts.statement: P. lakustai and P. perotorum are estimated to be about 5 meters long and weigh 2 tonnes.
facts.quote: The other species, P. lakustai and P. perotorum, have been estimated by Greg Paul at 5 m in length and 2 tonne in weight.

facts.statement: Pachyrhinosaurus was herbivorous and possessed strong cheek teeth batteries for cutting tough, fibrous plants.
facts.quote: They were herbivorous and possessed strong cheek teeth batteries to help them cut tough, fibrous plants.

facts.statement: Instead of horns, Pachyrhinosaurus skulls bore massive, flattened bosses over the nose and eyes.
facts.quote: Instead of horns, their skulls bore massive, flattened bosses: a large boss over the nose and a smaller one over the eyes.

facts.statement: P. canadensis and P. lakustai had two additional small, curved, backward-pointed horns on their frills.
facts.quote: In P. canadensis and P. lakustai, the frill bore two additional small, curved, backward-pointed horns.

facts.statement: It was previously thought that P. perotorum had unique forward-projecting horns, but 2019 research showed these were inaccurately reconstructed and it actually had backward-pointing horns like its sister species.
facts.quote: P. perotorum was thought to have two unique, flattened horns which projected forward and down from the top edge of the frill, but 2019 it was shown that these had been inaccurately reconstructed and it instead had the same backward pointed horns as its sister species.

facts.statement: In the Prince Creek Formation, P. perotorum engaged in niche partitioning with Edmontosaurus, preferring upland environments while the latter favored lowland deltas.
facts.quote: In the Prince Creek Formation, P. perotorum engaged in niche partitioning with Edmontosaurus; the latter favoured lowland deltas while the former preferred more upland environments.

facts.statement: Pachyrhinosaurus perotorum reached 28% of its adult body size by the age of one year.
facts.quote: When the animals were one year old, they had already reached 28% of their adult body size.

facts.statement: Pachyrhinosaurus perotorum was nearly half the size of a mature adult by the age of two.
facts.quote: By age two, they were almost half the size of a mature adult.

facts.statement: Pachyrhinosaurus perotorum did not reach its maximum size until approximately twenty years of age.
facts.quote: maximum size is not fully attained until about age twenty.

facts.statement: Sexual characteristics like pronounced nasal bosses in Pachyrhinosaurus perotorum developed at about nine years of age, likely corresponding to sexual maturity.
facts.quote: The development of characteristics useful in sexual selection, including competition between males, such as pronounced nasal bosses, occurred at approximately nine years of age.

facts.statement: Pachyrhinosaurus perotorum exhibits conspicuous growth banding in its bones, indicating slowed growth during winter months.
facts.quote: P. perotorum shows highly conspicuous growth banding in the bones, indicating retarded growth during the winter.

facts.statement: Pachyrhinosaurus lakustai does not show early growth banding in examined specimens, suggesting rapid growth in youth.
facts.quote: P. lakustai does not show growth banding early in ontogeny in the specimens that have been examined.

facts.statement: In Pachyrhinosaurus lakustai, sexual characteristics like nasal bosses appeared when the dinosaur was roughly 73% of its full adult size.
facts.quote: The development of characteristics useful in sexual selection, including competition between males, such as pronounced nasal bosses, occurred when the dinosaur was roughly 73% the size of a full-grown adult.

facts.statement: A Pachyrhinosaurus lakustai skull known as 'Harvey' had a massive lesion 195 mm in diameter on the right side of its face.
facts.quote: A skull of P. lakustai was found with severe lesions on the right side of the skull. The largest of these lesions was 195 mm in diameter, and harboured an additional large lesion inside it.

facts.statement: The severe lesions on the 'Harvey' specimen partially destroyed the right eye socket, likely causing blindness in that eye.
facts.quote: This hole also partially destroyed the right eye socket, which probably would've rendered the animal blind on that side.

facts.statement: Fossils from the St. Mary River Formation range geographically from Glacier County, Montana, to the Little Bow River in Alberta.
facts.quote: It ranges from as far south as Glacier County, Montana to as far north as the Little Bow River in Alberta.

facts.statement: The Horseshoe Canyon Formation, another source of Pachyrhinosaurus fossils, has been dated between 74 and 67 million years old.
facts.quote: The Horseshoe Canyon Formation has been radiometrically dated as being between 74 and 67 million years old.

facts.statement: The Horseshoe Canyon Formation was deposited during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous as the Western Interior Seaway withdrew.
facts.quote: It was deposited during the gradual withdrawal of the Western Interior Seaway, during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous period.
